brief: This weekly macro and derivatives flow note from UBS reports observed positioning across markets rather than building a single argued thesis. US equity flows turned constructive into the AI trade ahead of CPI, with buying in Semis, Memory and Hyperscalers; broader AI positioning is back to highs but Semis/Memory positioning still sits well below its prior peak. About $250m of January call premium hit US semis names including SNDK, AMD and CRWV. Asia semis flow was mixed: Taiwan buying led by TSMC, mixed Japan, outright Korea selling. Large SPX and SPY put spreads bought into CPI were quickly unwound once spot fell. Brazil (EWZ) and China-linked (HSTECH, KWEB, CSI, EEM) upside flows stayed constructive, though EWZ saw some early-week outright selling. Dollar selling exceeded expectations, with USDJPY downside buying, EUR topside interest, and CHF short-covering, though CHF positioning stays net short. ECB repricing after Thursday's meeting was the main rates move, worsened by stopped-out Euribor and steepener positions. Gold stayed bid on ETF demand, with GDX buying and near record-pace GLD buying despite higher rates and oil.
